result.title: General Frequency Principle for Linear Approximation Classes
result.summary: In this paper, we study a general frequency principle under gradient descent training for the finite linear approximation classes. Under suitable assumptions, we prove that the learner amplitude relative to the target amplitude vanishes at high frequencies, uniformly throughout training. We also establish sufficient conditions for low-frequency priority, covering single-frequency targets trained separately and two frequency components trained in the same run. This general frequency principle does not imply that lower frequencies always converge faster. Instead, for two frequencies that satisfy certain comparison conditions, one component will take longer to learn than the other; and in common cases, the longer component has higher frequency. Numerical experiments with Legendre and trigonometric bases validate the theoretical results.

AI.brief_summary: 该文在有限线性逼近类上研究梯度下降训练中的一般频率原理，证明高频处学习器振幅相对目标振幅在训练全程一致趋于零，并给出低频优先的充分条件与“学习更慢的分量通常频率更高”的比较结论，用 Legendre 与三角基数值实验验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其频率优先/谱偏置结论可能为 LVR 中视觉细节等高频信息能否进入内部状态、以及表示学习的收敛顺序提供分析视角，但需核查该线性逼近框架与深度 latent 推理动态的可迁移程度。
